newsitem.title: USA: Majority of Miami residents oppose city abolition.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Miami residents oppose city abolition.

text.p: Two-thirds of Miami residents oppose a move to abolish the city despite scandals at City Hall, poor services and a huge budget deficit, according to a poll released Sunday.
The Miami Herald-NBC 6 poll found that 66 percent of city residents oppose or are leaning against a proposal to abolish the city, with 20 percent in favor and 14 percent undecided.

The move to dissolve the city began in the wake of a corruption scandal that snared a city commissioner and the city manager, and the discovery that Miami faced a $68 million budget shortfall in the current fiscal year.
Abolition advocates collected enough petition signatures to force a referendum on the issue. The vote must be held by August, but no date has been set.

Miami residents cited culture and history as reasons to preserve the city and said they would opt in favor of Miami even though a merger with surrounding Dade County might provide them with lower taxes, the poll found.
The anti-abolition sentiment was particularly strong in the neighborhoods of Little Havana and Little Haiti, home to thousands of immigrants from Cuba and Haiti respectively.
Seventy-one percent of blacks and 69 percent of Cubans opposed abolition, while 49 percent of non-Hispanic whites were opposed.
"Miami is like a second homeland to me and it would hurt me very much if it were to disappear," Francisco Lopez, who move to Miami from Cuba 34 years ago, told the Herald.
The poll, of 848 randomly selected adults in the city, was conducted by telephone Jan. 24-29 and had a margin of error of plus or minus 3.5 percent.

Herald columnist Carl Hiaasen, a caustic critic who says City Hall has functioned as a "continuing criminal enterprise, though far less efficient than the Mafia or a drug cartel," lamented the poll's findings.
"Miami won't allow itself to be abolished," Hiaasen wrote. "Disgraced, mocked and stripped to the bone -- but not abolished."
